children: Cigarette company Altria said it was considering a takeover offer to buy its smaller London-listed peer Imperial Brands, creating a company valued at around $157 billion if a deal went ahead.

The U.S. tobacco and nicotine company said Thursday that any offer would be in cash and that it was also in talks with a third party to buy part of Imperial Brands if any deal went ahead. However, it said no agreement had been reached.

Altria didn't provide any financial details of the potential offer or about the third party. Altria had a market capitalization of $126.89 billion, while Imperial Brands was valued at 22.77 billion pounds ($29.87 billion) at close of business on Wednesday.
Imperial Brands didn't immediately respond to a request for comment on Altria's statement.

Imperial Brands shares were up 13% at 34.39 pounds in early afternoon European trading, a closing price not seen since July 2017, and were the biggest riser on the FTSE 100 index. Altria  shares closed at $76.28 on Wednesday. U.S. markets are closed for the Thanksgiving holiday.

Shares in Imperial Brands jumped earlier Thursday after Bloomberg reported that Japan Tobacco was interested in making a move for the U.K. company. According to Bloomberg, Japan Tobacco was considering a partnership to buy Imperial Brands, then splitting up the assets in different parts of the world. Talks were at an early stage, Bloomberg said.
Both companies declined to comment on the Bloomberg report.

Any deal would be a further blow to the London Stock Exchange, which has seen a wave of takeovers or companies switching their listings overseas. Most recently, low-cost airline easyJet agreed to a 5.7 billion-pound takeover by Global Management.
